Title: Savolitinib in Elderly Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Harboring MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutations: A Case Series
PMID: 
Authors: 

Abstract
Savolitinib is the first small-molecule inhibitor specifically targeting mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) tyrosine kinase approved in China. It is indicated for adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring MET exon 14 (METex14) skipping mutations for use as either first-line or subsequent-line therapy. Currently, there is limited real-world evidence on the long-term survival outcomes of elderly NSCLC patients (aged 65 years and above) with METex14 skipping mutations. In this report, we present three cases of elderly NSCLC patients with METex14 skipping mutations who were treated with savolitinib to evaluate its efficacy and safety in this population.

Case Description
The case series included three NSCLC patients harboring METex14 skipping mutations, aged 66 to 75 years, with comorbidities of Parkinson’s disease, hypertension, and breast cancer, respectively. They were treated with savolitinib as the second-line treatment after previously receiving AP regimens (pemetrexed + cisplatin). All patients achieved disease control according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST 1.1) within 2 months of initiating savolitinib (one with partial response and two with stable disease), and none showed disease progression. The progression-free survival (PFS) of the three patients was 15, 4, and 17 months, respectively.

Patient 1
A 67-year-old woman with no history of smoking was diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) (cT4N2M1) harboring a METex14 skipping mutation in June 2023. She had a decade-long history of Parkinson’s disease and no familial predisposition to the condition. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status at diagnosis was 2. Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry (IHC) using the 22C3 antibody showed a tumor proportion score (TPS) <1%. Computed tomography (CT) scans in May 2023 showed a soft-tissue mass in the left lung upper lobe and hilum of the lung, multiple nodules in both lungs, and enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes, suggesting lung cancer with mediastinal lymph node metastases and bilateral lung metastases (Figure 1A).
An AP regimen (0.5 g of pemetrexed on day 1, and 30 mg of carboplatin/cisplatin on days 1–3) was initiated in June 2023. The patient received one cycle of chemotherapy, but was then switched to savolitinib (400 mg once daily) due to severe gastrointestinal reactions. According to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0 (CTCAE v5.0), she developed grade 3 nausea and grade 2 fatigue during chemotherapy, which led to early discontinuation. The patient achieved stable disease (SD) after 2 months (Figure 1B) and continues to receive savolitinib to date. She had a progression-free survival (PFS) time of 15 months. She did not experience any treatment-related adverse events (AEs).

Patient 2
A 71-year-old woman with no history of smoking presented with chest pain and hemoptysis, and was diagnosed with right lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) stage IV NSCLC (cT4N1M1) harboring a METex14 skipping mutation. She had a history of hypertension and no family history of cancer. Her ECOG performance status at diagnosis was 2. In addition to hypertension, she had mild renal insufficiency (baseline creatinine 122 µmol/L), which limited her tolerance to platinum-based chemotherapy. PD-L1 IHC (22C3) revealed a TPS of 5%. CT scans revealed a cavitary mass located in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe of the lung, accompanied by multiple nodules in both lungs, indicative of lung cancer with bilateral metastatic involvement (Figure 2A). Subsequently, emission CT (ECT) scans showed increased uptake and enhancement in the body of the sternum, the right posterior 4th rib, and the 4th thoracic vertebra, suggesting a high possibility of bone metastases.
An AP regimen (0.6 g of pemetrexed on day 1, and 30 mg of carboplatin/cisplatin on days 1–2) was initiated in October 2023. After one cycle, the treatment was terminated due to severe gastrointestinal reactions. The patient experienced grade 3 diarrhea according to CTCAE v5.0, which required treatment discontinuation. She then switched to a savolitinib regimen (400 mg/day) in November 2023. The patient achieved partial response (PR) after two cycles and maintained tumor shrinkage within PR criteria for 4 months (Figure 2B). She had a PFS time of 4 months. She did not experience any treatment-related AEs.

Patient 3
A 66-year-old female with no history of smoking was admitted to hospital for treatment due to coughing and expectoration. She had a history of breast cancer and no family history of tumor. Her ECOG performance status was 2 at the time of NSCLC diagnosis. She had a long history of hyperlipidemia and mild hepatic steatosis, which may have contributed to chemotherapy intolerance. PD-L1 IHC (22C3) demonstrated a TPS <1%. In January 2023, a CT scan showed a mass in the right upper lobe of the lung measuring approximately 37 mm by 27 mm. A right upper lobectomy and mediastinal lymph node dissection were subsequently performed. The postoperative pathological diagnosis was stage IV NSCLC with pT2aN1M0 harboring an METex14 skipping mutation, with poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the right lung upper lobe, approximately 10% of which was sarcomatoid carcinoma. After radical resection for primary lesions and lymph node metastases, an AP regimen (0.8 g of pemetrexed on day 1 and 400 mg of carboplatin/cisplatin on day 1) was initiated in February 2023. After 5 months, the treatment was terminated due to bone metastases and adrenal metastases. During the preceding chemotherapy period, she experienced grade 2 vomiting and anorexia (CTCAE v5.0), which further reduced her tolerance to platinum-based therapy. She then switched to a savolitinib regimen (400 mg/day) in July 2023. She achieved SD after 3 months. As of the latest follow-up in August 2024, she achieved a PFS duration of 17 months without disease progression. During treatment, she developed grade 1 diarrhea, which was attributed to savolitinib. The dose was temporarily reduced to 200 mg once daily for 2 weeks, resulting in symptom resolution. After that, the original 400 mg daily dosage was successfully resumed without recurrence of diarrhea, indicating good long-term tolerability. The diagnostic and therapeutic courses of the three elderly patients are summarized in Figure 3.
All three patients had an ECOG performance status of 2 at the time of NSCLC diagnosis, and each presented with significant comorbidities—including Parkinson’s disease, cardiovascular risk factors, or a second primary malignancy—which collectively limited their tolerance to standard platinum-based chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations. All three patients weighed less than 50 kg and therefore received the recommended 400 mg once-daily dose according to the Chinese prescribing label. As of August 2024, the PFS durations were 15, 4, and 17 months, respectively. All three patients are currently continuing on savolitinib.
